passages.text: Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.
passages.sermon:
A wise man stands out from others.
A wise man understands the meaning of things.
Wisdom gives a man understanding.
Wisdom makes his face shine.
Wisdom changes his stern appearance.
Wisdom brings light and gentleness to his face.
passages.original: מִ֚י כְּהֶ֣חָכָ֔ם וּמִ֥י יוֹדֵ֖עַ פֵּ֣שֶׁר דָּבָ֑ר חָכְמַ֤ת אָדָם֙ תָּאִ֣יר פָּנָ֔יו וְעֹ֥ז פָּנָ֖יו יְשֻׁנֶּֽא׃

passages.text: Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.
passages.sermon:
A king rules over his people.
God gives the king authority.
You have made an oath before God.
You must obey the king’s command.
You must keep your promise to God.
passages.original: אֲנִי֙ פִּי־ מֶ֣לֶךְ שְׁמ֔וֹר וְעַ֕ל דִּבְרַ֖ת שְׁבוּעַ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Do not hasten to leave his presence, and do not persist in a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.
passages.sermon:
A king has great authority.
Do not rush to leave the king’s presence.
Do not persist in a bad cause before the king.
The king will do whatever he wants.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּבָּהֵ֤ל מִפָּנָיו֙ תֵּלֵ֔ךְ אַֽל־ תַּעֲמֹ֖ד בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע כִּ֛י כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַחְפֹּ֖ץ יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: For the king’s word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
passages.sermon:
The king holds supreme authority.
His word has power over all.
No one can question the king.
No one can say to him, "What are you doing?"
passages.original: בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דְּבַר־ מֶ֖לֶךְ שִׁלְט֑וֹן וּמִ֥י יֹֽאמַר־ ל֖וֹ מַֽה־ תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.
passages.sermon: A person who obeys the king’s command will not experience harm.\r\nA wise person understands the right time for action.\r\nA wise person knows the proper way to act.
passages.original: שׁוֹמֵ֣ר מִצְוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵדַ֖ע דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט יֵדַ֖ע לֵ֥ב חָכָֽם׃

passages.text: For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.
passages.sermon:
Every purpose has a right time.
Every purpose has a right procedure.
A man often suffers much misery.
This misery weighs heavily on him.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לְכָל־ חֵ֔פֶץ יֵ֖שׁ עֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּֽי־ רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם רַבָּ֥ה עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?
passages.sermon: No one knows what will happen in the future.\r\nNo one can tell a person what will come next.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אֵינֶ֥נּוּ יֹדֵ֖עַ מַה־ שֶּׁיִּֽהְיֶ֑ה כִּ֚י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽהְיֶ֔ה מִ֖י יַגִּ֥יד לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
passages.sermon:
No person can control the wind.
No one can hold the wind back.
No person has power over the day of death.
No one can escape death when it comes.
No one can leave the battle during war.
Wickedness cannot free those who do evil.
Evil will not save the one who commits it.
passages.original: אֵ֣ין אָדָ֞ם שַׁלִּ֤יט בָּר֙וּחַ֙ לִכְל֣וֹא אֶת־ הָר֔וּחַ וְאֵ֤ין שִׁלְטוֹן֙ בְּי֣וֹם הַמָּ֔וֶת וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁלַ֖חַת בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־ יְמַלֵּ֥ט רֶ֖שַׁע אֶת־ בְּעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: All this I have seen, applying my mind to every deed that is done under the sun; there is a time when one man lords it over another to his own detriment.
passages.sermon:
I have seen all these things.
I have paid close attention to every action done under the sun.
Sometimes, a person rules over another person.
This power harms the one who rules.
passages.original: אֶת־ כָּל־ זֶ֤ה רָאִ֙יתִי֙ וְנָת֣וֹן אֶת־ לִבִּ֔י לְכָֽל־ מַעֲשֶׂ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֧ט הָאָדָ֛ם בְּאָדָ֖ם לְרַ֥ע לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then too, I saw the burial of the wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they had done so. This too is futile.
passages.sermon:
I saw wicked people.
They died.
People buried them.
These wicked people used to enter the holy place.
They walked there often.
People in the city praised them for what they did.
People forgot their evil deeds.
This is meaningless.
passages.original: וּבְכֵ֡ן רָאִיתִי֩ רְשָׁעִ֨ים קְבֻרִ֜ים וָבָ֗אוּ וּמִמְּק֤וֹם קָדוֹשׁ֙ יְהַלֵּ֔כוּ וְיִֽשְׁתַּכְּח֥וּ בָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר כֵּן־ עָשׂ֑וּ גַּם־ זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.
passages.sermon:
Solomon is the speaker.
Solomon observes life under the sun.
Sometimes, people do evil things.
The punishment for their evil is delayed.
The authorities do not carry out justice quickly.
Because of this delay, people’s hearts change.
People become determined to do more evil.
They see that evil is not punished right away.
This encourages them to continue doing wrong.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁר֙ אֵין־ נַעֲשָׂ֣ה פִתְגָ֔ם מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה מְהֵרָ֑ה עַל־ כֵּ֡ן מָלֵ֞א לֵ֧ב בְּֽנֵי־ הָאָדָ֛ם בָּהֶ֖ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רָֽע׃

passages.text: Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.
passages.sermon:
A sinner may do evil many times.
He may do evil a hundred times.
He may still live a long life.
But I know something else.
It will go well for people who fear God.
These people show reverence before God.
God will bless those who honor Him.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֹטֶ֗א עֹשֶׂ֥ה רָ֛ע מְאַ֖ת וּמַאֲרִ֣יךְ ל֑וֹ כִּ֚י גַּם־ יוֹדֵ֣עַ אָ֔נִי אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִהְיֶה־ טּוֹב֙ לְיִרְאֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽירְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.
passages.sermon: The wicked do not fear God.\r\nIt will not go well for the wicked.\r\nTheir days will not become long like a shadow.
passages.original: וְטוֹב֙ לֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע וְלֹֽא־ יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִ֖ים כַּצֵּ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֵינֶ֥נּוּ יָרֵ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: There is a futility that is done on the earth: There are righteous men who get what the actions of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the actions of the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futile.
passages.sermon:
People live on the earth.
Sometimes, things happen that do not make sense.
Some people are righteous.
These righteous people sometimes receive what should happen to the wicked.
Some people are wicked.
These wicked people sometimes receive what should happen to the righteous.
This is not fair.
I see this.
I say this is also meaningless.
passages.original: יֶשׁ־ הֶבֶל֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשָׂ֣ה עַל־ הָאָרֶץ֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ יֵ֣שׁ צַדִּיקִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מַגִּ֤יעַ אֲלֵהֶם֙ כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָרְשָׁעִ֔ים וְיֵ֣שׁ רְשָׁעִ֔ים שֶׁמַּגִּ֥יעַ אֲלֵהֶ֖ם כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הַצַּדִּיקִ֑ים אָמַ֕רְתִּי שֶׁגַּם־ זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: So I commended the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this joy will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God gives him under the sun.
passages.sermon:
Solomon is the speaker in this passage.
Solomon is a wise king.
Solomon commended joy.
He said there is nothing better for a person under the sun.
A person should eat.
A person should drink.
A person should be glad.
This joy will go with him in his work.
This will last all the days of his life.
God gives these days to him under the sun.
passages.original: וְשִׁבַּ֤חְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ אֶת־ הַשִּׂמְחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵֽין־ ט֤וֹב לָֽאָדָם֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כִּ֛י אִם־ לֶאֱכ֥וֹל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת וְלִשְׂמ֑וֹחַ וְה֞וּא יִלְוֶ֣נּוּ בַעֲמָל֗וֹ יְמֵ֥י חַיָּ֛יו אֲשֶׁר־ נָֽתַן־ ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth—though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night— I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.
passages.sermon:
I set my heart to know wisdom.
I wanted to understand what happens on earth.
People work hard day and night.
They do not even see sleep with their eyes.
I saw all the works of God.
No one can understand all that God does under the sun.
A person may work hard to find the meaning.
He will not find it.
Even if a wise man says he knows,
He cannot truly understand.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤תִּי אֶת־ לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת חָכְמָ֔ה וְלִרְאוֹת֙ אֶת־ הָ֣עִנְיָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י גַ֤ם בַּיּוֹם֙ וּבַלַּ֔יְלָה שֵׁנָ֕ה בְּעֵינָ֖יו אֵינֶ֥נּוּ רֹאֶֽה׃ וְרָאִיתִי֮ אֶת־ כָּל־ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִים֒ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוּכַ֜ל הָאָדָ֗ם לִמְצוֹא֙ אֶת־ הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשָׂ֣ה תַֽחַת־ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ בְּ֠שֶׁל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲמֹ֧ל הָאָדָ֛ם לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָ֑א וְגַ֨ם אִם־ יֹאמַ֤ר הֶֽחָכָם֙ לָדַ֔עַת לֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִמְצֹֽא׃
